title: Starlake LLM migration readiness discovery
summary: Initial discovery for migrating inference from an OpenAI + vLLM stack to Redwood. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary concerns are performance parity with TGI/vLLM, encryption/KMS, SOC2 logs, and cost predictability. Agreed to run a two-week pilot with parity evals; Redwood to share security pack and a benchmark harness template.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: Date: 2027-03-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Alicia Morgan, Devon Patel, Sofia Ramos (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Carlos Ruiz, Priya Nair, Ethan Lowe (Starlake)

[00:03] Alicia Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro — I'm Alicia on the account side, Devon and Sofia are our SEs. How are we doing in terms of agenda?

[00:11] Maya Chen: Hi, yeah thanks. We wanted to walk you through what we're running today and what a parity eval would look like from our side. We've been on OpenAI for the last 18 months and recently added vLLM for localized inference to cut costs.

[00:24] Devon Patel: Great, can you give a quick run of the current infra — model sizes, traffic pattern, and any hard SLOs you have?

[00:31] Carlos Ruiz: Sure. Primary models are a 13B instruct family and a 70B for high-precision tasks, running in vLLM on prem for the 13B and TGI-based endpoints in our Azure account for the 70B. Peak qps is ... uh, around 250 reqs/min for interactive and batch overnight jobs for embeddings. Latency SLOs: p95 under 450ms for interactive.

[00:51] Sofia Ramos: Okay so a mixed deployment, vLLM on-prem and TGI/managed on Azure. Are you using any prefix caching or KV cache today?

[00:57] Ethan Lowe: We built a small prefix cache layer; it's rudimentary. KV cache is enabled in vLLM for the 13B. For the 70B on Azure we rely on TGI's caching plus some application side caching.

[01:10] Priya Nair: Security quick note: everything must be KMS-backed, keys rotated quarterly, and audit logs stored for 365 days. We also need SSO via Okta and RBAC. SOC2 is baseline.

[01:22] Alicia Morgan: Understood. Redwood supports KMS integrations, SSO, RBAC, and long retention for audit logs in dedicated/private. We'll share our SOC2 docs and the security pack post-call.

[01:32] Maya Chen: Two main questions: 1) Can you hit parity with our vLLM/TGI latency and accuracy? 2) What's the cost delta if we move off our vLLM cluster to Redwood Dedicated?

[01:45] Devon Patel: For parity, we typically do a short evaluation where we run your prompt set and metrics against our hosted or dedicated runtime. We do need the prompt set and a few sample traffic patterns. For latency, a lot depends on kernel selection and batching — our runtime has some continuous batching strategies but we can tune for low-latency SLOs.

[02:04] Carlos Ruiz: One worry — we've seen different tokenization and slight output variation between OpenAI and Anthropic, and then TGI sometimes returns different logits. How do you handle model-compat differences?

[02:15] Sofia Ramos: Good point. We do two things: model mapping to compatible variants (e.g., a Redwood-verified 13B family) and a prompt/response normalization layer for eval parity. For strict parity we run A/B on the same seed/temperature and capture metrics like exact-match, BLEU-ish, and custom business metrics.

[02:35] Maya Chen: Do you support function calling and structured output similar to OpenAI? We use function calling heavily.

[02:40] Devon Patel: Yes, our API supports function/tool calling patterns and structured JSON outputs. There are occasional differences in how the model behaves with implicit prompts; the eval will surface that.

[02:50] Priya Nair: If we go dedicated or private, how do you manage KMS? We can't have customer keys leave our control.

[02:58] Alicia Morgan: Dedicated has KMS integrations that let you either use a cloud KMS or bring your own keys via HSM in private deployments. For private we can deploy with your vault behind the VPC and HSM controls so keys never leave your network.

[03:12] Ethan Lowe: And what about model artifacts? We need guarantees that model weights and any customer data in logs are not shared.

[03:18] Sofia Ramos: We separate control and data plane. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and data plane isolation. Private is fully customer controlled. Logs can be configured to ship to your log bucket or stay in your VPC. We'll send a diagram for that.

[03:31] Carlos Ruiz: Can we talk about the pilot? We want to prototype with the 13B first, run throughput and latency tests, and do an accuracy sweep.

[03:38] Devon Patel: Typical pilot we propose: two-week run, ingest your prompt set, run comparators against your vLLM/TGI baseline, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/cost, and accuracy metrics. We'll provide a harness — a lightweight k6/ab-style runner or a Python harness.

[03:55] Maya Chen: That sounds good. One more: how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity? Our load is spiky with marketing promos and model retraining windows.

[04:04] Sofia Ramos: Dedicated offers configurable autoscaling with predictable warm pools and burst credits. Hosted can handle spikes but you'll see variable costs. Private you control autoscaling but will need ops to manage capacity.

[04:20] Priya Nair: Compliance: is there an option to have audit logs forwarded to our SIEM without storing sensitive prompts? We need redaction options.

[04:27] Alicia Morgan: Yes, we have redaction pipelines and can forward structured logs to your SIEM. We can exclude full prompt text or hash it, and retain metadata for audits. We'll include details in the security pack.

[04:40] Carlos Ruiz: On the cost side, what's the rough delta moving from our current vLLM nodes to Redwood Dedicated? We want a ballpark to evaluate ROI.

[04:48] Devon Patel: Ballpark depends on utilization. If you're running at higher utilization, Redwood Dedicated often can be 20–35% lower unit cost due to batching and kernel optimizations. We'll run your usage profile through our cost model during the pilot and give exact numbers.

[05:06] Maya Chen: Are there known compatibility gotchas when porting from vLLM to Redwood? We've hit tokenization differences, kv-cache miss behaviors, and sometimes TGI plugins that don't map cleanly.

[05:17] Sofia Ramos: The common gotchas: tokenizer mismatch, caching semantics (how you warm or reuse KV cache), and certain TGI custom endpoints. We typically do a mapping exercise early — provide a compatibility matrix and scripts to normalize.

[05:35] Ethan Lowe: For the 70B work, we might want to keep it on Azure for cost reasons and only move the 13B to Redwood. Is hybrid supported?

[05:43] Alicia Morgan: Absolutely. Hybrid routing is a common pattern — route certain workloads to dedicated/private and keep large batch models on your cloud provider. Our routing rules can be per-route or per-customer.

[05:55] Carlos Ruiz: Show of hands: what do you need from us to get the pilot kicked off?

[06:01] Devon Patel: We'll need: 1) a representative prompt set (10–20K prompts is good), 2) traffic profile (qps, burst patterns), 3) access or artifact to reproduce your vLLM runtime behavior — ideally a small container or runbook, 4) your evaluation metrics and thresholds.

[06:18] Maya Chen: We can share the prompt set and traffic logs. We can't give you keys to our production vLLM cluster but we can provide traces and samples.

[06:25] Priya Nair: Security requirement: we need an NDA addendum for the pilot and a network architecture diagram before we create accounts.

[06:32] Alicia Morgan: Noted. We'll start an NDA addendum today. We'll also share a baseline network diagram and the SOC2 pack.

[06:40] Sofia Ramos: A few technical clarifications: are you using multinode sharding for the 13B? Are you running any quantized 4-bit runtimes?

[06:47] Ethan Lowe: Yes, the 13B is using 4-bit quant with bitsandbytes in vLLM, single-node mostly but with a small pool for high availability.

[06:56] Devon Patel: We support quantized paths and 4-bit execution — we'll want to match your quantization config in the pilot. There's sometimes a small accuracy delta with 4-bit; we'll measure that.

[07:08] Carlos Ruiz: Can Redwood run our evals with the same random seed and temperature to reduce nondeterministic differences?

[07:13] Sofia Ramos: Yes, we can set deterministic sampling where supported and mirror temperature/seed. Some ops may still differ but it reduces variance.

[07:22] Maya Chen: Regarding the harness, can you provide an example that invokes function calls and streaming responses? That's a critical path for us.

[07:29] Devon Patel: We'll include a Python harness that demonstrates streaming and function calling along with CI-friendly metrics reporting.

[07:36] Priya Nair: For auditability, can you include request/response digests instead of full plaintext in logs?

[07:42] Alicia Morgan: Yes — digesting and hashing options are supported. We'll include recommended redaction rules.

[07:49] Ethan Lowe: One small thing — latency percentiles for sessions that use KV cache matter a lot; we've seen big differences in p99 with cold cache. Can you simulate cold-start scenarios?

[07:58] Sofia Ramos: We can. Pilot plan will include cold-start tests and warm-cache tests, and we'll capture p50/p95/p99 across those buckets.

[08:10] Carlos Ruiz: Mentioning competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and a couple startups doing runtime tuning. Any customers with similar setups?

[08:18] Devon Patel: We have customers who've replaced mixed OpenAI/vLLM stacks; we'll anonymize references but can share a case study.

[08:26] Maya Chen: Ok let's go through a quick recap and next steps.

[08:31] Alicia Morgan: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2/security pack, pilot harness, and network diagram. Starlake to share prompt set, traffic profile, and evaluation metrics. Legal to run NDA addendum. Goal: start pilot in two weeks.

[08:44] Priya Nair: Can we get the security pack by Friday? We need time for internal review.

[08:49] Alicia Morgan: Yes, we'll send it by Friday.

[08:52] Maya Chen: Pilot ramp — two-week pilot, then a 1-week analysis and results review?

[08:58] Devon Patel: That timing works. We'll provision a dedicated pilot environment and run the harness with you.

[09:05] Carlos Ruiz: Any blockers for us on the Redwood side?

[09:09] Sofia Ramos: Only the prompt set and traffic profile. Also we'd like a short sample of vLLM logs to understand caching patterns.

[09:18] Ethan Lowe: We'll put together those artifacts.

[09:22] Alicia Morgan: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for pilot kickoff and attach the security pack and NDA.

[09:30] (Meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional background noise at 00:40, speaker attribution may be approximate for a few exchanges, some proper nouns (TGI, vLLM) occasionally mis-capitalized.
